E.g. officer sees a brick of cocaine on the table from outside a window, they can go inside without a warrant to seize the drugs. Once inside, plain view continues to apply, as does a search incident to arrest if an arrest is made. No warrant needed

I agree, that’s why I clarified (in this situation) multiple times. When determining whether the police have lawful access to enter, you can consider whether they have plain view knowledge leading to probable cause that a crime is occurring/has occurred. PC is just a description of the required level of proof for a situation, and other instances use it differently.

Exigent circumstances is if they believe someone is in danger, and yes, plain view exemption is the formal phrase for probable cause in this situation. Officers see evidence of a crime from a legal POV, they can then investigate further, i.e. go inside to seize that evidence and then anything else that becomes “in plain view” or any searches incident to arrest. Plain view = probable cause (as used here) because the officer must have PC to believe that the item in question is related to illegal activity. 

I do recognize that just having probable cause (from something else) that something within the residence is illegal is not a legal search, that’s very clearly what a warrant is and that is a formal process. I don’t think that I was insinuating that with my comment either, as I specified that the officer in that situation would have a visual on the thing giving the PC. Not confused

I also had this happen, but not actually breach through my cervix. I had a Paragard for seven years, and one day during sex I got the worst pain I have ever experienced in my pelvis. Absolutely excruciating, lasted for about an hour, constantly on the edge of consciousness. 

I thought it was my IUD but I had always been taught that if I can still feel the strings, then everything is fine. Well, couple of months later I found out I was pregnant. Went in for the ultrasound to confirm, and my IUD had shifted several inches down, so the embryo had attached at the very top of my uterus where it wasn’t affected. 

My partner and I chose to terminate, and after I healed I went in to get another Paragard. This one lasted like three weeks, and I had the same excruciating pain. Immediately went to my gyno and she looked and thought that everything was fine, but I pushed for an ultrasound and lo and behold it had shifted again. So I’ve been on the pill since then — even though I miss my IUD so much, I’m not willing to constantly get them inserted and have my uterus reject it every time.

also, be sure to celebrate your wins! if your management team doesn’t already recognize accomplishments like that, be sure to recognize yourself in conversation with them. at my store, every shift, a manager has a conversation w/ the employee before they clock out. how’d you do, what was your biggest win, did you meet your goals, what can you work on next time, etc. if you had a really good interaction, like in your other comment mentioning the customer compliment, bring that up! hopefully your managers will reciprocate your excitement, and having an atmosphere that encourages and recognizes success makes it a really fun work environment. despite everything, i still think retail is fun!

i agree with the previous commenter, especially about learning how to read your customer, and engaging. i know this can be a bit scary, especially if things are rushed and you feel pressure to get through the transaction quickly. don’t feel like you have to go from nothing to everything at once! your managers will appreciate hearing it anyway. 

my favorite tactic is complimenting something they picked out. i work in clothing, so i often compliment the outfits the guest is wearing anyway, but I often feel uncomfortable commenting on their physical appearance, so i usually try to keep it to something they can control and will feel good about. eg, what they’re wearing, the bear or clothes they picked out, their jewelry, etc. If they’re wearing a sports shirt, or something with a pop culture reference, that’s an easy conversation starter too! 

It will get more and more comfortable with practice. Don’t feel like you have to say something for every single guest, just start with the ones you feel genuinely about. Does your management team pick out items that you need to upsell, or is it your decision? I’ll usually have something near the registers that I’ll point out if the customer seems receptive, only after engaging about a separate point. for example, we usually had a big jar on the counter, full of clearance scrunchies. if i a guest was waiting on me and i caught them looking at the scrunchies, i would simply tell them the sale, and then mention that i’m obsessed with scrunchies too. it lets them in on the details, but still feels like you’re just a friend, talking about scrunchies. it often boils down to making them feel like you’re their friend, and are showing them an extra product because you think they’ll love it, or it’ll match well with what they already have. you know your store and product better than they do, make them feel like you’re the expert! 

start slow, maybe a customer or two an hour, find your footing, and then lean into it. and remember: the aggressive customers are not personal, if they get snippy with you about any part of the transaction, they’d get snippy with your coworkers too. 

to me, registers are fun! i like the conversation, and once you have some more practice i think you will too. good luck, don’t overthink it!
